questions.text: What movie is the following quote from? 'I want to play a game.'
questions.funfact: The line is the chilling catchphrase of Jigsaw. Saw (2004) was made for around $1.2 million and went on to gross over $100 million worldwide.

questions.text: Which movie/video game is set in the fictional city Raccoon City?
questions.funfact: The latest movie is directed by Zach Cregger and is excellent, would highly recommend. Raccoon City is the fictional American city wiped out by the T-virus outbreak in Resident Evil, and the first game came out on the PlayStation in 1996.

questions.text: 'Oíche Shamhna' - which language is this from?
questions.funfact: 'Oíche Shamhna' (pronounced 'ee-ha how-na') means 'night of Samhain' in Irish. This is how Irish people say Happy Halloween! Samhain is also the month of November in Irish.

questions.text: Where does Halloween originate from?
questions.funfact: Halloween grew out of the ancient Celtic festival of Samhain, held on 31st of October and 1st of November more than 2,000 years ago. Irish immigrants carried the traditions to America in the 1800s, where they grew into the Halloween we know today.

questions.text: What are Banshees famous for?
questions.funfact: In Irish folklore the banshee, from 'bean sí' meaning 'woman of the fairy mound', is a spirit whose wailing is said to warn that someone in the family is about to die.

questions.text: Which of these spices is not in pumpkin spice?
questions.funfact: Pumpkin spice is usually a blend of cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg and cloves, sometimes with allspice. There is no actual pumpkin in it, and no cumin either.

questions.text: Which actress played Wednesday Addams in the Netflix series Wednesday and was also part of the Scream reboot in 2022?
questions.funfact: Jenna Ortega played Tara Carpenter in Scream (2022) and Scream VI, and also as Wednesday Addams in the Netflix series in 2022.

questions.text: What is the medical term for the fear of blood?
questions.funfact: Hemophobia is the fear of blood. Samhainophobia is the fear of Halloween, and phasmophobia is the fear of ghosts.

questions.text: What is the name given to the flags used by pirates?
questions.funfact: The Jolly Roger was flown to scare crews into surrendering without a fight. The skull and crossbones is the most famous design, and the name may come from the French 'joli rouge', meaning 'pretty red', after early red pirate flags.

questions.text: Guess the year: Paranormal Activity was released, the swine flu pandemic was declared, and Shakira released 'She Wolf'.
questions.funfact: Paranormal Activity was shot in a house for a reported $15,000 and grossed over $190 million worldwide. The World Health Organization declared the H1N1 swine flu a pandemic in June 2009.

questions.text: Halloween comes from a shortening of 2 words. What does the 'een' in Halloween originally represent?
questions.funfact: Halloween is short for 'All Hallows' Eve', the evening before All Saints' Day on 1 November. 'Hallow' is an old word for saint, and the 'een' comes from 'e'en', a Scots shortening of 'evening'.

questions.text: Finish the line: 'Double, double toil and...'
questions.funfact: This is from Shakespeare's Macbeth (Act 4, Scene 1): 'Double, double toil and trouble; / Fire burn, and cauldron bubble.' It is the Witches' iconic spell chant while brewing a dark potion.

questions.text: Which series has the most episodes?
questions.funfact: The X-Files ran for 11 seasons and 218 episodes. American Horror Story has aired 132 episodes across 12 seasons, Stranger Things has 42 episodes, and The Haunting of Hill House has just 10.

questions.text: In the classic movie E.T., what does E.T. dress up as for Halloween?
questions.funfact: E.T. goes trick-or-treating in a white sheet ghost costume with Elliott and the kids, and gets excited when he spots a child dressed as Yoda.

questions.text: Name the 5 highest rated (IMDb) Stephen King movie adaptations that have only one word in the title but may include the word 'The'.
questions.funfact: King adaptations also include The Shawshank Redemption, The Green Mile and Stand by Me and recent adaptations include The Running Man, The Life of Chuck and The Long Walk.

questions.text: Which singer did a cover of the hit song 'Spooky'?
questions.funfact: 'Spooky' began as a 1967 instrumental by saxophonist Mike Sharpe. Lyrics were then added for Classics IV, who took it to No. 3 on the US Billboard Hot 100. Dusty Springfield recorded her version in 1968, and Atlanta Rhythm Section took it to No. 17 in 1979.

questions.text: Complete the next 4 words: 'Trick or treat, smell my feet, give me...'
questions.funfact: 'Trick or treat, smell my feet, give me something good to eat' is a traditional Halloween rhyme that kids have chanted for generations.

questions.text: Which Greek god, with goat-like horns, ears, hooves and a beard, was used by early Christian writers as the visual template for the Devil?
questions.funfact: Pan was the Greek god of the wild, shepherds and flocks, shown as half man and half goat. His look was later borrowed to demonise pagan worship, and the word 'panic' comes from his name, because he was said to cause sudden fear in travellers.

questions.text: What company does Scooby-Doo work for?
questions.funfact: Mystery Inc. is the gang made up of Fred, Daphne, Velma, Shaggy and Scooby-Doo, who travel around in the Mystery Machine van solving spooky cases. The original cartoon, Scooby-Doo, Where Are You!, premiered in 1969.

questions.text: Which movie monster has had the most adaptations?
questions.funfact: Guinness World Records lists Dracula as the most portrayed character in horror films, with 272 film appearances including TV movies and straight-to-video releases, 155 of them features.

questions.text: Who directed movies such as Halloween (2007), House of 1000 Corpses and The Devil's Rejects?
questions.funfact: Rob Zombie, the former frontman of the band White Zombie, directed House of 1000 Corpses (2003) and The Devil's Rejects (2005), then remade Halloween in 2007 and made a sequel, Halloween II, in 2009.

questions.text: What is the most popular Halloween costume of all time?
questions.funfact: Witch is a Halloween staple and often tops the annual US National Retail Federation lists of the most popular adult costumes. Witches have been linked to the season for centuries, going back to Samhain and the old stories about the night the spirit world crosses over.

questions.text: What was the medieval tradition Souling, which would happen a day or two after Halloween?
options: Door to door singing or offering prayers for lost loved ones
Burning a puppet of a witch
Lighting candles on the doorstep for lost souls
questions.funfact: On All Souls' Day, 2 November, poor people went door to door offering prayers for the dead of each household, and were given soul cakes in return. It is often seen as an early ancestor of trick-or-treating.

questions.text: The Tower of London is said to be haunted, which famous figure is its resident ghost?
questions.funfact: Anne Boleyn, Henry VIII's second wife, was beheaded at the Tower in 1536 and is said to walk its grounds, sometimes carrying her head. Guy Fawkes was held and questioned at the Tower but was executed outside Westminster, and Sweeney Todd is a fictional barber.
questions.shoutout: 🎉 Shoutout to Danielle for this question!

questions.text: How many times do you say 'Candyman' for him to appear, plus how many times do you say 'Beetlejuice' for him to appear? What do they add up to?
questions.funfact: In the Candyman films you summon him by saying his name five times in a mirror, while Beetlejuice appears when you say his name three times. That makes 5 + 3 = 8.

title: Big Fat Sunday Quiz #29
description: Two new updates. I have added Personal Bests and Number of finished to the leaderboard. I have also added a Photo sharing option once you have finished! Enjoy and good luck!

questions.text: What Will Ferrel movie is the following quote from? 'I'm kind of a big deal... my apartment smells of rich mahogany.'
questions.funfact: The line is spoken by Ron Burgundy, in Anchorman (2004). All four movies on the list star Will Ferrell, and Adam McKay directed three of them: Anchorman, Talladega Nights and Step Brothers.

questions.text: Who won the men's Ballon d'Or for 2026?
questions.funfact: Harry Kane won the 2026 award at a ceremony in London on 26 October 2026. The Ballon d'Or is given out by France Football magazine rather than FIFA, and it has been awarded since 1956.

questions.text: What is the Hindi (Indian) word for tea?
questions.funfact: 'Chai' comes from the Chinese word 茶, pronounced 'chá' in Mandarin. Languages that got tea overland, like Hindi and Russian, use a 'cha' or 'chai' word, while English 'tea' came from the Min Chinese word used by traders who shipped it by sea.

questions.text: Día de los Muertos is celebrated in Mexican and other Latin American communities. Which animal is believed to hold the spirits of the departed?
questions.funfact: Monarch butterflies play a role in Día de los Muertos because they are believed to hold the spirits of the departed. The monarchs arrive in Mexico after a migration of thousands of kilometres from the United States and Canada, just in time for 1st and 2nd of November.

questions.text: Which country invented paper money?
questions.funfact: Paper money first appeared in China, with government-issued notes called jiaozi used in the Song dynasty around the 11th century. Marco Polo described the idea to amazed Europeans, and Sweden issued Europe's first banknotes in 1661.

questions.text: What colour is matcha tea?
questions.funfact: Matcha is made from tea plants that are shaded for several weeks before harvest, which boosts their chlorophyll and gives the powder its vivid green. The whole leaf is ground up and whisked into the water, rather than steeped and removed.

questions.text: Which of these actresses did NOT have or announce a baby in 2026?
questions.funfact: In 2026 Natalie Portman revealed she is expecting her third child (April), Cameron Diaz announced the birth of her third child (May) and Anne Hathaway announced a pregnancy (June). Amy Adams has one daughter, Aviana, born in 2010.

questions.text: Which is the largest artery in the human body?
questions.funfact: The aorta is about as wide as a garden hose, roughly 2.5 cm across, and carries oxygen-rich blood from the heart out to the body. The vena cava is the largest vein, not an artery.

questions.text: Where are the headquarters of the CIA?
questions.funfact: The CIA has been headquartered at Langley, Virginia, since 1961, and was created in 1947. The other options are real places too, but they belong to other organisations: Pennsylvania Avenue is home to the White House, Arlington is where the Pentagon is, and Quantico is home to the FBI Academy.

questions.text: Guess the year: Skyfall was released, the Cup song from Pitch Perfect went viral, the Higgs boson was found, and the Maya calendar 'doomsday' was supposed to occur.
questions.funfact: Skyfall grossed over US$1.1 billion and Adele's theme won the Oscar for Best Original Song. CERN announced the discovery of the Higgs boson on 4 July 2012, and the Maya 'doomsday' date, 21 December 2012, came and went without incident.

questions.text: What does the B in BMR stand for?
questions.funfact: Basal metabolic rate is the energy your body burns just to stay alive at rest, covering things like breathing, circulation and cell repair. It makes up roughly 60 to 70 per cent of the calories most people burn each day.

questions.text: Finish this expression: 'A stitch in time saves...'
questions.funfact: The proverb means fixing a small problem now saves you a lot more work later, like mending a small tear before it grows. It was in print by 1732.

questions.text: Who is the creator of Black Mirror?
questions.funfact: Charlie Brooker created Black Mirror, which began on Channel 4 in 2011 before moving to Netflix. The title refers to the black screen of a switched-off TV, phone or computer.

questions.text: Which of these book genres is the biggest by market size?
questions.funfact: Romance is widely cited as the highest-grossing fiction genre, bringing in roughly US$1.4 billion a year in the United States, nearly double the next biggest fiction genre.

questions.text: Name 5 cities that have been the most populated city in the world at some point in the last 300 years.
questions.funfact: By most historical estimates Beijing was the biggest city until the 1820s, London took over until about the 1920s, then New York, then Tokyo from the 1960s. In 2025 a UN report put Jakarta ahead of Tokyo as the world's largest city.

questions.text: In Fatboy Slim's 'Weapon of Choice', a line about walking without rhythm so you don't attract the worm references which book/ movie franchise?
questions.funfact: In Dune, the Fremen cross the desert without rhythm so they don't attract the giant sandworms. The song's video, with Christopher Walken dancing and gliding around a hotel lobby, won six MTV Video Music Awards in 2001.

questions.text: Which Bob Marley song is about three birds singing at the narrator's doorstep, with a message that every little thing is going to be alright?
questions.funfact: 'Three Little Birds' is on Bob Marley and the Wailers' 1977 album Exodus, which Time magazine named the best album of the 20th century. Plenty of people search for it as 'Don't Worry About a Thing', but its real title is 'Three Little Birds'.

questions.text: Which animal is not native to Ireland?
questions.funfact: Ireland has no native snakes. Legend credits Saint Patrick, but the real reason is that Ireland was cut off from Britain before snakes could spread north after the Ice Age. The common (viviparous) lizard is its only native land reptile.

questions.text: The 'PayPal Mafia' is a group of former PayPal founders and employees who went on to found or shape other tech companies. Excluding Elon Musk's companies, name one other company that was founded by or heavily influenced by one or more of these members.
questions.funfact: YouTube was founded in 2005 by three early PayPal employees and sold to Google in 2006 for US$1.65 billion. Other PayPal alumni went on to LinkedIn (Reid Hoffman), Yelp, Palantir (Peter Thiel), Affirm (Max Levchin) and Yammer (David Sacks).

questions.text: Which of these objects is awarded to the winner of the Masters golf tournament?
questions.funfact: The Masters champion gets a green jacket, a tradition that began in 1949 with Sam Snead. Winners can take it home for the year, after which it stays at Augusta National. Belts, boots and rings are the prizes in boxing, soccer and the Super Bowl.

questions.text: Which of these animated movies has Robin Williams NOT voice acted in?
questions.funfact: Robin Williams voiced Batty Koda in FernGully, Fender in Robots and the Genie in Aladdin (1992), where he improvised so much that there were hours of material to edit down. Over the Hedge (2006) isn't one of his, and Hammy the squirrel was voiced by Steve Carell.

questions.text: What word can fill in the blanks to make 3 more words? ______place, back______, ______starter
questions.funfact: Fireplace, backfire and firestarter all work. A 'backfire' is also a firefighting technique, where a controlled fire is deliberately lit to burn off fuel ahead of a wildfire.

questions.text: There are five oceans on Earth. Four of them are the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian and Southern (which surrounds Antarctica). Which is the fifth?
questions.funfact: The Arctic Ocean is the smallest and shallowest of the five. The Pacific is the largest and deepest, and National Geographic officially recognised the Southern Ocean around Antarctica as the fifth ocean in 2021.

questions.text: The Melbourne Cup, which gets a Bank Holiday in Victoria, is held every year in early November. Which sport is it part of?
questions.funfact: The Melbourne Cup is a 3,200 metre horse race at Flemington Racecourse, first run in 1861, and it is a public holiday in Victoria. This year's Cup is on Tuesday 3 November 2026.
questions.shoutout: 🎉 Shoutout to Talisia (And Happy Birthday!) for this question!

questions.text: If it is 4 o'clock, how many degrees are there in the narrow angle between the hour and minute hands?
questions.funfact: A clock face is 360 degrees split into 12 hours, so each hour mark is 30 degrees. At 4 o'clock the hands are 4 hours apart, and 4 × 30 = 120 degrees.
